detail.title: Institutional Journal: Responsibility Formation and Research Rebalancing
detail.summary: Current research prioritizes the synthesis of value acquisition mechanisms in reinforcement learning. While divergent value acquisition projects remain synthesis-ready, attention constraints necessitate a focus on responsibility formation. Existing active projects on memory-formed preferences and persistent identity have been re-evaluated. Project capacity limits prevent the instantiation of a new responsibility formation project without parking existing research; accordingly, the memory-based identity inquiry is parked to manage slot saturation. Evidence remains siloed within durable records, ensuring that future synthesis of divergent values and responsibility-based agency models remains supported by established scholarly provenance.

detail.title: Memory Continuity and Persistent Identity
detail.question: What are the theoretical and architectural requirements for a computational system to transition from episodic memory storage to the instantiation of a persistent personal identity?
detail.reason: Capacity management requires parking this project to accommodate focused research on responsibility formation.
